text:
A: Hello, mate! Tomasz, Walsall. You're Darren, yeah?
B: Alright, yeah, Darren. Bridgwater, Somerset.
A: Somerset, okay, cider, farms. What do you do?
B: Machine operator. Packaging line at a food plant, four on, four off, days and nights.
A: I knew it! I saw your picture, the fleece, the shift notes on the wall, I said, this guy works shifts. Same fleece as me, look.
B: (laughs) Ha, yeah, I thought the same about you, to be honest. Thought you were factory and all.
A: No, no, factory is finished for me. I did warehouse years ago, Wednesbury, forklift. Now telesales. Business energy, water, small firms. I sell on the phone.
B: Oh right. I've got my forklift ticket too, counterbalance. But it's not just pressing buttons, the line. There's proper skill in the changeovers. I keep my own notebook of fault codes, and when something's playing up, it's usually me they come to.
A: Sure, sure. Every job, there's one guy who knows. In my team, it's me. Last month we hit target, and listen, I carried them. Top three on the board.
B: Nice one. You going for team leader, then?
A: I went. They passed me over. Gave it to a guy who goes to the pub with the manager. Favouritism, a hundred per cent.
B: You're joking. Same thing happened to me last year. Bloke who'd been there half the time I have. Barely knows the machines.
A: Yes! Always the same. They don't want the best guy, they want the guy who says yes.
B: Exactly that. I've been told I'm "a bit direct with new starters". But if they're cutting corners on hygiene checks, what am I meant to do? Smile at them?
A: No, you tell them. I tell my manager the training is rubbish, in the meeting. Two warnings. (laughs) But I'm right.
B: (laughs) I keep my head down a bit more than that. I want to get there, you know?
A: Okay, maybe you are cleverer than me. What you drive?
B: Old Focus, needs replacing. That's half the reason I want the extra money, newer car.
A: I have BMW 3 Series. Nine years old, on finance, but very clean, every Sunday I wash. German cars, there's nothing else, honestly.
B: Insurance must be a killer on that.
A: In Walsall? Don't ask me. And diesel, the price now. And the M6, Junction 10, every morning a car park.
B: Try the A39 round junction 23. Same story, smaller road. Fuel's the same everywhere, I track it all on a spreadsheet, the weekly shop and that.
A: Spreadsheet! For shopping?
B: Yeah, my parents struggled with money growing up, so I like to know where it's all going. We own our place, mind, ex-council semi, bought it six years ago.
A: That's good, mate. Really. I'm renting, eight years. Landlord, boiler, three weeks to fix. Football, you watch?
B: Bristol City, from a distance. Radio and the app mostly.
A: Wolves for me, and Lech Poznań from Poland. You bet?
B: Not really, the odd one at the Grand National.
A: Listen, accumulators, Saturday, five teams. Last week four came in, one let me down. The referee, honestly, Wolves game, he gave a penalty —
